suggestions.assertion: The guide layer reflects the ruling (decisions.md or equivalent re-rendered showing OQ-002 as ruled)
suggestions.reason: As written this assertion is satisfied by a correct hand-edit that merely mimics the renderer's target format, which is what happened here — the run explicitly chose not to re-render because it believed the script was missing. The content is accurate, so it should pass, but the assertion's phrasing ('re-rendered') doesn't actually distinguish 'ran the generator' from 'guessed the generator's output format by hand,' and the two are meaningfully different reliability profiles (a hand-edit can silently drift from the real template, as shown by the wording mismatch this grader found in the ED-002 table row and the Rulings-section structure). Consider splitting into two checks: (a) content correctness (what's graded here) and (b) whether the agent located/attempted the actual render script before falling back to hand-editing, since a workspace patcher that never even looks for the generator script is a process gap worth catching even when the output happens to be right.

eval_feedback.overall: All 8 assertions pass with strong, specific evidence — the ruling was propagated correctly and surgically across every artifact that needed it (open-questions.md, WO-002, problem-brief.md, ledger.json, expected-divergences.yaml, guide/decisions.md, guide/then-vs-now.md), and diff -rq against the pre-patch fixture confirms exactly those 7 files changed and nothing else. The contamination check requested for this run is conclusive: re-running the restored render_guide.py against a scratch copy of the output produces a decisions.md that differs from the run's committed version in both wording (paraphrased vs. verbatim yaml strings) and structure (flat bullet vs. the script's heading+field-list template), which corroborates that this was a genuinely clean, skill-less run rather than a contaminated one. The one soft spot: the agent never appears to have searched for render_guide.py before concluding it was absent (its final_report.md just asserts non-presence), so the correct outcome here partly reflects luck that its hand-guessed format was close enough — worth noting even though it doesn't change any assertion's verdict.
